label: token right after an early "e" (positions 1-2)
explanation: Fires during the original phase at step 1 or 2 when the previous input was "e", i.e. on the token right after an "e" that sits at position 0 or 1. Every such step activates (dev precision 1.0), and these steps hold 99.7% of the activation mass. Magnitude is highest at t=2 after "e e" (e.g. "e e l" reaches the max). Steps after a first-position "e" are typically about 0.7-0.8 of max, and after "x e" at t=2 about 0.6-0.8. The current token makes little difference, although "l" is slightly higher. Missed steps are tiny activations (under 0.1 of max), mostly the step after a first-position "g" or the step right after an "e"-triggered firing. It does not fire after an "e" at position 2 or later: t=3 after "e" is rare and weak. It also does not fire at t=0, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase.

issues: Minor: the explanation says missed steps are 'under 0.1 of max', but some t=3 misses after an 'e e' pair at positions 1-2 reach about 0.3 (e.g. '1 e e [b:0.32]'). The t=3 & prev=e & rel_tok(-2)=e class has precision 0.42 on test but carries only about 0.09% of the mass, so it is negligible.

All other claims check out. Test false positives = 0. Misses hold 0.4% of the mass. Activations are 0 at t=0, there is 1 step on the delimiter, 15 tiny steps in the copy phase and 412 weak steps at t=3 (dev). The max (1.00) is 'e e l' at t=2. Steps after a first-position 'e' are about 0.69-0.82, and after 'x e' about 0.58-0.82. 'l' has a higher rate (1.7x lift).
